title: Senate GOP Blocks Bid to Limit Trump's Iran War Powers Despite Midterm Backlash
snippet: In a 51-48 vote, Senate Republicans defeated a War Powers Resolution targeting President Trump's military campaign in Iran, standing by the administration despite growing public dissatisfaction and recent election losses.
content:
Capitol Hill — Senate Republicans held the line on Thursday, sinking a Democratic-led effort to rein in President Donald Trump’s war authority in Iran. The 51-48 vote effectively blocked a War Powers Resolution that would have required the administration to end military actions or obtain explicit authorization from Congress to continue the conflict.

The near party-line vote came just weeks after voters delivered sweeping victories to Democrats in the midterm elections, a political shift widely driven by public exhaustion over the ongoing war and its strain on the national economy. Only three Republicans—Sens. Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, and Rand Paul of Kentucky—broke ranks to vote with Democrats. Meanwhile, Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania was the sole Democrat to vote alongside Republicans against the resolution.

Rising Financial Costs and Public Fatigue

The measure marks the 21st time lawmakers have voted on a war powers resolution since the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran launched on February 28. Recent polling from Reuters/Ipsos shows public support for the war hitting a low of just 31%, reflecting widespread frustration across the electorate.

Democrats argued that the administration has dragged the nation into a costly, aimless conflict without constitutional sanction. Pentagon data released in late October revealed that military spending for the campaign has already surpassed $47 billion—more than 25% above initial Defense Department estimates from July. Opponents of the conflict pointed out the stark contrast between foreign defense spending and domestic budget cuts to safety net programs like healthcare subsidies and subsidized school meals.

"Its unpopularity was made absolutely, manifestly clear in the election results," said Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine of Virginia on the Senate floor prior to the vote, linking the conflict directly to inflation and skyrocketing prices for energy and groceries.

Looming Clash in the Next Congress

Thursday's vote follows a September victory for the resolution in the House, where it passed 220-204. While an earlier iteration of the measure passed both chambers of Congress earlier this year, the Trump White House dismissed it, claiming the action was not legally binding.

However, the political landscape is set for a dramatic shift on January 3, when Democrats take control of majorities in both the House and Senate. Democratic leaders have vowed to make ending the Iran war their top legislative priority, setting up an inevitable legislative showdown with the White House in the coming year.
